age.evidence: Paper does not state age of subjects explicitly.

sex.evidence: The water behavioral economics experiment used a cohort of 8 rats (n = 4 male; n = 4 female), and the food behavioral economics experiment used a separate cohort of 14 rats (n = 7 male; n = 7 female). For photometry experiments, two cohorts were run separately and their data were combined (combined n = 5male,n = 3 female).

dosing.doses_raw: 0.8 mg/kg i.p. (behavioral economics); cumulative 400 µg/kg × 3 = 0.4/0.8/1.2 mg/kg (auditory-cued task); cumulative 500 µg/kg × 2 = 0.5/1.0 mg/kg (lever-cued task)
dosing.evidence: DOI (0.8 mg/kg i.p) or vehicle (saline) were given 25 min prior to test sessions... 3 cumulative DOI doses were given as a series of 3 injections (400 µg/kg, i.p. for each injection)... 2 cumulative DOI doses were given as a series of 2 injections (500 µg/kg, i.p. for each injection)... 2,5-Dimethoxy-4-iodoamphetamine (DOI, Cayman) was dissolved in sterile saline vehicle.

day_night_flipped.evidence: maintained on a 12:12h reverse light-dark cycle (ZT0 at 1900) and experiments were performed during the dark cycle.

assays.assay_name: Behavioral economics operant task (food and water)
assays.assay_description: Within-session escalating fixed-ratio operant task in Med Associates chambers, 30 min sessions of 10 × 3-min bins, separate cohorts pressing for water or food pellets. Outcomes: rewards earned per price, Q0 (consumption at low cost), α (demand elasticity). DOI (0.8 mg/kg) vs saline in within-subject counterbalanced design.

application_type.evidence: DOI (0.8 mg/kg i.p) or vehicle (saline) were given 25 min prior to test sessions

setup_habituation.evidence: No specific pre-test apparatus habituation described.

setup_restrain.evidence: Experiments were conducted in individual sound-isolated standard experimental chambers; rats freely moving.

food_restriction.evidence: For conditions using food reward, rats were mildly food restricted to maintain a stable weight of ~95% free feeding weight

water_restriction.evidence: For conditions using water reward, rats were water restricted ~23 hours prior to the experiment

time_to_assay.evidence: DOI (0.8 mg/kg i.p) or vehicle (saline) were given 25 min prior to test sessions

sample_size.evidence: water behavioral economics experiment used a cohort of 8 rats (n = 4 male; n = 4 female), and the food behavioral economics experiment used a separate cohort of 14 rats (n = 7 male; n = 7 female).

outcomes.summary: DOI (0.8 mg/kg) produced bidirectional effects on reward value at low prices: decreased Q0 for food but increased Q0 for water. DOI increased demand elasticity (α) for both rewards, indicating reduced motivation at high costs regardless of reward type. No significant sex × drug interactions.
outcomes.statistics: Q0 Reward × Treatment interaction F(1,20)=7.429, p=0.013; Food Q0 p=0.041; Water Q0 p=0.0042; main effect of Drug on α F(1,20)=16.37, p=0.0006.
outcomes.evidence: DOI decreases Q0 for food (p = 0.041) but increases Q0 for water (p = 0.0042)... DOI increases economic demand elasticity (α)... for both water and food reward (main effect of Drug, F(1, 20) = 16.37, p = 0.0006).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Rewards earned at each price, Q0, α, and food/water consumption.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: within-session, escalating-price design wherein fixed ratios (FRs) were increased across the 30 min session comprised of 10 three-minute bins

B4_ethological.evidence: Operant lever pressing, not ethological behaviours.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Instrumental operant task requiring learned action-outcome contingencies.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med Associates beam-break / standard operant data collection.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Univariate ANOVAs and curve fits; no PCA/clustering.

E1_environment_type.evidence: standard experimental chambers (25 × 27 × 30 cm; Med Associates)

E6_spatial.evidence: Single operant chamber with lever and reward port.

E7_social_context.evidence: Experiments were conducted in individual sound-isolated standard experimental chambers

E8_food_water.evidence: completion of FRs resulted in activation of syringe pumps delivering 95 uL of water... or the delivery of (2) 45 mg food pellets

D1_continuity.evidence: each subject received DOI or saline on alternate test days, separated by a retraining session

D2_session_duration.evidence: 30 min session comprised of 10 three-minute bins

D3_recording_days.evidence: DOI and saline test sessions on alternate days.

D4_baseline.evidence: Saline session is a comparator under drug condition; no pre-drug baseline within same assay reported for analysis.

D5_followup.evidence: Acute testing only; no ≥24 h post-drug behavioural recording.

D6_circadian.evidence: 30 min session; does not span ≥6 h.

judge_notes: Three distinct behavioural paradigms retained: (1) behavioural economics operant task (food + water cohorts), (2) auditory-cued Pavlovian water task with photometry, (3) lever-cued Pavlovian task with photometry (food + water). Did not split food vs water cohorts because the rubric specifies different reinforcers within the same paradigm are still one assay.

Fiber photometry was retained as a behavioural readout context (animals were performing tasks), but per the rubric the photometry recording itself is a neural readout; behavioural measures (latency, poke probability, lever press time) are scored. B1 counted only behavioural measures, not dopamine signal measures.
DOI doses consolidated to 0.4, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2 mg/kg across cumulative dosing series and the behavioural economics 0.8 mg/kg dose.
Group housing scored 'no' based on consistent candidate agreement citing single-housing in supplementary methods; light cycle 'yes' (reversed) is supported by quoted methods.

D4 baseline scored 'Yes' for photometry assays because vehicle control sessions are recorded within the same within-subject crossover design and used as baseline; for the behavioural economics assay, the vehicle session functions similarly but is a separate test day rather than a pre-drug baseline within the same session, scored 0 conservatively.
E8 food/water scored 'Yes' for all assays because reward (food pellets or water drops) is delivered into the apparatus during the recording session and is accessible to the animal.

B1 measures: Behavioural economics has 4-6 measures (rewards/price, Q0, α, consumption at multiple FRs) → score 2; auditory Pavlovian primarily 2-3 behavioural measures (latency + poke probability across trial types) → score 1; lever Pavlovian has 4-6 measures (lever press time, poke probability, proximal latency, distal latency, by reinforcer) → score 2.
